extendedData.note: Eheieh ('I Am') and Al-Ahad ('The Absolutely One') both express the primordial divine self-subsistence that transcends all numerical or relational sense.
Eheieh as pure undifferentiated being parallels Al-Wahid, the foundational divine unity from which all multiplicity derives.
As-Samad (the Eternal, self-sufficient Absolute needing nothing) mirrors Eheieh's quality of pure self-subsisting existence at the crown of being.
Yah as the divine name of Chokmah (Wisdom) parallels Al-Alim (The All-Knowing), both representing divine omniscience as the first expression of divine consciousness.
Chokmah means Wisdom; Al-Hakim (The Wise) is the divine name most directly corresponding to the quality of divine wisdom.
Al-Khabir (The All-Aware, perceiver of inner realities) resonates with Chokmah's quality of immediate, penetrating divine awareness.
YHVH Elohim as the name of Binah, the great form-giver, parallels Al-Khaliq (The Creator) — both express the divine act of bringing structured existence into being.
Al-Bari (The Originator who differentiates and individuates forms) closely mirrors Binah's role as the womb that separates and gives discrete identity to the undifferentiated seed of Chokmah.
Al-Musawwir (The Fashioner of Forms) is the most direct Islamic parallel to Binah's function as the divine matrix that gives form to all things.
El as the name of Chesed (Mercy, boundless love) parallels Ar-Rahman (The Most Gracious), the all-encompassing divine mercy that extends to all creation without condition.
Ar-Rahim (The Most Merciful, intimate mercy toward those who turn to God) reflects the active, relational mercy that is a core quality of Chesed.
Al-Karim (The Most Generous) mirrors El/Chesed as the divine name of overflow, grace, and magnanimous giving.
Al-Wahhab (The Bestower, who gives freely without expectation of return) resonates with Chesed's quality of pure, unconditional divine generosity.
Al-Wadud (The Loving/Most Affectionate) corresponds to the loving-kindness (chesed) that is the essential quality of the fourth Sephira.
Al-Jabbar (The Compeller, whose will cannot be resisted) directly parallels Elohim Gibor (Mighty God) as the name of Geburah's irresistible divine force.
Al-Qahhar (The Subduer who dominates all things absolutely) resonates with Geburah's quality of divine severity that reduces all resistance to submission.
Al-Aziz (The Almighty/Invincible) mirrors the Gibor (Mighty/Heroic) quality of Elohim Gibor — divine power that cannot be overcome.
Al-Qawi (The Strong) expresses the same martial divine strength contained in Geburah's name Elohim Gibor.
Al-Muntaqim (The Avenger/Requiter of injustice) parallels Geburah as the sphere of divine retributive justice that corrects and balances the scales.
An-Nur (The Light) is the most resonant Islamic parallel to Tiphareth, the solar Sephira of beauty and illumination — the light at the centre of the Tree of Life.

Al-Haqq (The Truth/The Real, reality itself) resonates with Tiphareth's divine name including Da'ath (Knowledge/Reality) and Tiphareth's role as the sphere of the solar logos — the truth at the heart of existence.
Al-Fattah (The Opener/Victor) parallels YHVH Tzabaoth as the name of Netzach (Victory) — both express the divine quality of triumph and breaking through resistance.
Ar-Razzaq (The Provider of sustenance) resonates with Netzach as the sphere of nature's teeming abundance and the instinctual drive toward nourishment and desire.

As-Sami (The All-Hearing) parallels Hod as the sphere of communication, reception, and the Mercurial capacity to receive and transmit — both express divine attentiveness to the forms of language and thought.
Al-Basir (The All-Seeing) mirrors Hod's quality of divine intelligence that perceives and structures all visible and mental forms.
Al-Hayy (The Ever-Living, self-subsisting divine life) directly parallels El Chai (The Living God) in Shaddai El Chai — the divine name of Yesod as the sphere of the vital life-force.
Al-Qayyum (The Self-Subsisting Sustainer, the ontological ground of existence) resonates with Yesod as the Foundation — the support and basis upon which Malkuth rests.

Adonai ('My Lord/King') and Al-Malik (The King/Sovereign) are the most direct cross-traditional parallel — both are royal divine names expressing sovereignty over the manifest creation (Malkuth = The Kingdom).
Malik al-Mulk (The Possessor of All Sovereignty/Owner of the Kingdom) is a compound divine name whose meaning directly mirrors Adonai ha-Aretz — the Lord of the Kingdom/Earth.
Az-Zahir (The Manifest/The Outwardly Evident, the divine apparent in all things) parallels Malkuth as the sphere of divine manifestation and material reality — the domain of Adonai ha-Aretz.
